doc.title: David Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 18, 2003

title: Upcoming plans and closing
summary: Mixing his album, Carnegie Hall with strings, planned recordings, his son's college search, and thanks.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well what’s in the near future for you? I know you’re mixing another album.

Well the near future is to mix this album. I’m playing Carnegie Hall on the fourteenth with my quartet with strings so I’m using ten — this time I’m using ten string players from New York. I hope they execute as well as the Cubans. I’m going to do this gig in Seattle I have to waste my time on doing. I probably will do a recording with Taj Mahal and Ishmael Reed, another Gwo-Ka with Kip Hanrahan. I think that’s on the books for October. November and December I’ll just probably be doing some gigs with the Gwo- Ka Masters. This little period of time right in here I’m concentrating on getting my kid in to a decent college. We’ll see, maybe he’ll wind up here.
Maybe so. We’d be happy to have him. Well it’s been fascinating talking to you and having you on campus.
Oh I’m looking forward to playing the concert.
You are a very creative man.
Well this is a great place to be. I’m happy to have done this interview with you. Thank you.
I’ll look forward to the dinner tonight. Thank you.
